title: Oklahoma and Big Chief
summary: Allen asks about Oklahoma; Lewis recalls Big Chief and being on the road.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: A little worse? Well I don't think they become much worse than you ever did. Well, we won't question you on that. What was it like being in Oklahoma? Well Oklahoma, it reminds me of it. See they've got a lot of them, and a lot of things. Well I'll tell you about, that's why I met Big Chief. You ever met Big Chief? Yeah I met him. The big Indian? Yeah. Yeah. Don't let him stand nobody's who tell you, set the bears on fire, you understand?
The big fat guy that played trombone, outside of his mouth.

He's playing on that number I played a while ago, Someday You'll Be Sorry with Lewis Armstrong and all the bone. Yeah, well that guy man. Sure, you see, when you're a trooper up and down the road like I was, like Alvin Walz and the bands like that, you run into everything. You run into everything. And the guy is just another member, you know, who turns your brother, and they sit in there and play.
